items.author: MeteorologistChristopherNunley
items.text: TROPICAL STORM ISELLE INCREASES CALIFORNIA T-STORM CHANCES THURSDAY AND FRIDAY THIS WEEK🌀🌴🌧️ ⛈️a plume of deep tropical and subtropical moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Iselle will be pulled northward into California Thursday and especially Friday as an upper-level trough approaches the West Coast! While this is not expected to be a widespread rain event, moisture levels will increase considerably and scattered showers and storms could develop across portions of the state. On Thursday, tropical moisture begins spreading into Central and Southern California. There is around a low to medium chance for showers across portions of Southern California, the Central Coast and Bay Area while isolated activity will also be possible farther inland. Most locations will remain dry, but brief showers, sprinkles or virga could develop almost anywhere beneath the moisture plume. Thunderstorm chances Thursday remain low but non-zero. The combination of tropical moisture, heat and instability means an isolated heavier shower or thunderstorm cannot be completely ruled out Thursday. Gusty and erratic winds could also occur near showers or virga. The better opportunity for precipitation arrives Friday as the approaching Pacific Northwest trough taps directly into the subtropical moisture plume. Shower chances expand northward into the Sacramento Valley where much of the Valley now has a low to medium chance for rain showers. The Sierra Nevada should have the best opportunity for meaningful precipitation with thunderstorm probabilities increasing Friday. Localized flooding is possible in the Sierra Nevada. This is a classic low-probability, potentially higher-impact setup.  Most Californians probably won't see measurable rain, but any isolated thunderstorm that develops within this unusually moist and unstable environment could produce locally heavier rain, lightning and gusty winds🌀🌴🌧️ ⛈️
